newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-GERMANS MISSING KEY PLAYERS AGAINST NORTHERN IRELAND.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-GERMANS MISSING KEY PLAYERS AGAINST NORTHERN IRELAND.

text.p: European champions Germany will be missing several of their Euro 96 heros when they bid to end a disappointing run of results against Northern Ireland in Saturday's group nine World Cup qualifier.

Libero Matthias Sammer, defender Thomas Helmer and midfielders Mario Basler, Dieter Eilts and Christian Ziege have all been ruled out because of injury as the Germans aim to beat the province for the first time for nearly 20 years.
The Germans often have problems against teams who adopt the physical and fast style of football played in the English and Scottish leagues where most of the Northern Ireland squad make their living.

The last times they beat Northern Ireland was in 1977, a 5-0 victory in Cologne when present coach Berti Vogts was still playing. Two defeats followed in European championship qualifiers in 1982 and 1983 in Belfast and Hamburg.
Their last two clashes have ended in draws, including a 1-1 in a friendly in Belfast just before this year's Euro 96 triumph.

"We are going to have to take the game to Northern Ireland who have a physical game," said Vogts who was particularly disappointed by Thursday's late withdrawal of defensive midfielder Eilts with a knee injury.
"Dieter is a rock for us and an important player for our system. I now have to think who is going to replace him."

VfB Stuttgart's Thomas Schneider has been impressive in training and could win his first cap in place of Eilts. Karlsruhe's Michael Tarnat is tipped to start his first international in Ziege's place on the left side.

Borussia Dortmund's Stefan Reuter is expected to take over the libero role with Bayern Munich's Thomas Strunz operating as a wing-back on the right-hand side. Both players can switch positions, however.
Germany - Andy Koepke, Stefan Reuter, Juergen Kohler, Thomas Strunz, Markus Babbel, Thomas Schneider, Michael Tarnat, Thomas Haessler, Andy Moeller, Fredi Bobic, Juergen Klinsmann.
